topics.label: Lecture opening and framing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing, welcoming students and contextualizing the lecture on complement.

topics.label: Fundamentals of the complement cascade
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational principles, nomenclature conventions, and central biochemical role of C3 that organize the complement system.

topics.label: Complement recognition and activation pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the upstream pathways through which complement detects pathogens and deposits convertases to reach the activation threshold.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream effector functions through which activated complement destroys pathogens and amplifies the immune response.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins that protect host cells by suppressing accidental complement activation and membrane attack complex assembly.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how genetic and acquired deficiencies across different complement components produce distinct clinical presentations and disease susceptibilities.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic analyzes the evolutionary strategies and molecular mechanisms used by pathogens to circumvent complement attack.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing, concluding the lecture and previewing the next topic in the series.
